summary.text: India is the world's largest producer and consumer of pigeonpea, accounting for roughly 65% to 70% of global production. Over the 3-year baseline period (2021–22 to 2023–24), India’s annual tur production has fluctuated between 3.30 and 4.25 million metric tonnes (MT) (averaging ~3.5 to 3.8 million MT), delivering a combined 3-year national output of approximately 10.8 to 11.4 million MT.

protection.name: Fusarium Wilt (Fusarium udum)
protection.geography: All-India Black Soil Belts (Heavy in Maharashtra, Karnataka, MP)
protection.impact: Soil-borne systemic wilt; leaves turn pale yellow, wilt, and droop; internal xylem shows a prominent purple-black vascular streak extending up the stem beneath the bark; partial wilting of only one side of the plant is common; field mortality ranges from 20% to 100%.
protection.passage: Pigeon Pea — source table 125, row 2. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Sterility Mosaic Disease (SMD) / "Green Plague" (Pigeonpea Sterility Mosaic Virus transmitted by eriophyid mite Aceria cajani)
protection.geography: National Epidemic Hazard (Devastating in Marathwada, Deccan, UP)
protection.impact: Leaves become severely reduced in size, displaying bright green mosaic mottling; severe stunting and bushy proliferation of vegetative shoots ("witches' broom" appearance); total cessation of flowering and pod formation, leaving plants completely sterile.
protection.passage: Pigeon Pea — source table 125, row 3. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Gram Pod Borer (Helicoverpa armigera) & Spotted Pod Borer (Maruca vitrata)
protection.geography: Major Flowering & Podding Belts (All Commercial Belts)
protection.impact:
Helicoverpa: Larvae chew large, clean, circular holes in green pods, feeding on seeds with half their body exposed.

Maruca: Larvae web together flowers, leaves, and pods into dense clusters, feeding protected inside the webs.
protection.passage: Pigeon Pea — source table 125, row 4. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Pod Fly (Melanagromyza obtusa)
protection.impact: Small shiny black fly inserts eggs directly into the green pod wall; white maggots feed entirely inside developing seeds, creating shallow feeding furrows; seeds rot or become shriveled, discolored, and unmarketable; adults emerge leaving tiny circular pinholes.
protection.passage: Pigeon Pea — source table 125, row 5. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Phytophthora Stem Blight (PSB) (Phytophthora cajani)
protection.impact: Water-soaked dark brown-to-black lesions on main stem and branch bases; lesions girdle the stem; bark sloughs off, foliage wilts rapidly, and plants snap at the collar; occurs in low-lying patches after heavy monsoon rains.
protection.passage: Pigeon Pea — source table 125, row 6. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Pulse Beetle / Bruchid (Callosobruchus chinensis, C. maculatus)
protection.impact: Adults lay small whitish eggs on dried pod/seed surfaces; grubs bore inside cotyledons, hollowing out grains and leaving round exit holes; destroys seed germination and milling recovery.
protection.passage: Pigeon Pea — source table 125, row 7. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.
